endorsements.quote: Clearly define who bears responsibility if AI-suggested changes negatively impact patient care—whether it is the vendor, the health care institution, or a combination.
Understand and follow applicable guidelines when introducing these features [ 11 ].
Consider periodic third-party evaluations of AI systems and processes, focusing on data handling, software quality, and patient safety standards.
We need to maintain comprehensive records of all AI-generated recommendations and subsequent human-validated changes.

Although AI can autonomously recommend changes to database configurations or workflows, no modifications should be pushed into production without human review and authorization (particularly for Tiers II–IV).
Ensure all data in transit or at rest is encrypted.
Only after thorough testing and clinician feedback should changes move to production.

unlisted_practices: Restrict authority to approve AI-recommended changes to designated administrators, informaticists, or clinicians with appropriate privileges.
Provide manual build and backout steps with every AI-recommended change.
Deploy AI-generated configuration changes in a nonproduction environment first and validate for unintended effects, usability impacts, and conflicts.
Implement continuous automated regression testing of clinical workflows, alert systems, and data integrity after each AI-prompted change.
Provide clear explanations for each AI configuration recommendation to aid human reviewers.
Use robust deidentification or anonymization methods when EHR data is used to train AI models.
Align AI-driven EHR changes with interoperability standards such as HL7, FHIR, SNOMED CT, and LOINC.
Ensure AI solutions handling protected health information comply with federal regulations, documenting access, role-based permissions, and breach reporting mechanisms.
Incorporate liability and responsibility allocation into institutional policies and vendor contracts.
Use secure protocols to protect patient and system information when AI accesses external data sources and registries.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework paper proposing the 'Elastic EHR' five-tiered model for AI integration, governance, and maintenance in EHR systems, without empirical data collection or evaluation.
